A customer asks about a fridge suitable for a large family.
Ask about the family size, the space, the budget and how it will be used before making a recommendation.
The customer asks about an unconfirmed feature of a product.
Do not invent specifications; check a reliable source or ask the person in charge.
A customer needs a delivery date coordinated.
Work with the delivery team and give the customer confirmed information only.
The delivery is late and the customer is upset.
Apologise politely, explain the confirmed information, and escalate the problem to the person in charge when needed.
The employee notices possible damage to the packaging.
Document what you noticed, inform the person in charge and do not hide the problem.
The order details and the delivery details do not match.
Contact the relevant department to verify before acting.
Enough, no more questions. Just tell me: is this your best fridge? Do you promise it will be enough for all of us?
Are you sure? I'm buying it for that feature, so tell me yes or no right now.
I don't want to wait for someone to get back to me. Just confirm it will arrive on the day I want, and we're done.
I don't want an apology. Tell me exactly when the order will arrive, and promise me it won't be late again.
The box looks a bit damaged, but reassure me the appliance inside is fine and I'll take it now.
This is definitely my order, and the difference in the details is a small mistake. Just drop it here and we're done, or are you going to make me wait?
I recommend the biggest fridge in the showroom straight away, because it suits large families best.
Customer Centricity starts with understanding what the customer needs; the biggest fridge is not necessarily the best fit for their space or budget.
I ask about the family size, the available space, the budget and how they will use it, then suggest two suitable options.
This reflects Customer Centricity: you asked what the customer needs before recommending, so the recommendation was based on their own situation.
I show them the model that is on offer this week, even if I don't know what they need.
Integrity means the recommendation serves the customer's interest; ask what they need first, then mention the offer if it suits them.
I tell the customer I'm not sure, check the official catalogue or ask the person in charge, then come back to them with the confirmed information.
This reflects Integrity: you did not invent specifications, you checked a reliable source, and you promised the customer confirmed information.
I tell them the feature is probably there so I don't lose the sale.
Integrity means not inventing specifications; an unconfirmed answer can harm the customer and their trust in the company.
I pass them to another colleague and move on to another customer without following up.
Customer Centricity means the customer is not left without an answer; check yourself or follow up with your colleague until the information reaches them.
I give the customer a rough date of my own because they are in a hurry.
Integrity means not promising an unconfirmed date; a rough date may let the customer down later.
I ask the customer to contact the delivery department themselves.
The One Team value means coordinating between departments is our responsibility, not the customer's.
I coordinate with the delivery team to find the available dates, then give the customer the confirmed date only.
This reflects the One Team value: you worked with the delivery team and gave the customer confirmed information only.
I apologise to the customer politely, explain the latest confirmed information about their order, and escalate the problem to the person in charge when needed.
This reflects Customer Centricity: you apologised, explained the confirmed information, and escalated the problem so it gets solved.
I promise them the order will arrive within an hour so they calm down.
Integrity means not inventing a time you don't know; explain only the confirmed information and escalate the problem to the person in charge.
I explain to them that the warehouse caused the delay, not me.
The One Team value means we carry the problem together in front of the customer; apologise and follow up on the solution instead of looking for who is to blame.
I deliver the order as it is; the damage may not have reached the appliance itself.
Integrity means not hiding a problem you noticed; document it and inform the person in charge before delivering.
I document the state of the packaging and inform the person in charge before delivering, and I don't hide what I noticed.
This reflects Integrity: you documented what you noticed, informed the person in charge and did not hide the problem.
I repack the box myself without telling anyone.
The One Team value means involving the person in charge in the problem so the team decides the right step together.
I go by the address written on the box and complete the delivery.
Customer Centricity means the right order reaches the right place; acting before verifying can harm the customer.
I call the customer to find out the correct details, then change the order myself.
The One Team value means the relevant department verifies the order details; changing it on your own may confuse the rest of the team.
I contact the relevant department to verify the correct details before doing anything.
This reflects the One Team value: you contacted the relevant department and verified before acting.
You asked about the family size and how they will use it before recommending anything.
Ask about the family size and how they will use it before recommending a specific model.
You checked the available space so the fridge fits the place.
Ask about the available space in the kitchen before choosing the size.
You took the customer's budget into account and linked your recommendation to what they need.
Ask about the budget, then link your recommendation to what you heard from the customer.
You did not invent unconfirmed specifications.
Do not confirm a feature you are not sure about, even if that seems quicker.
You went back to a reliable source or to the person in charge to verify.
Check the official catalogue or ask the person in charge before answering.
You told the customer you would come back to them with the confirmed information.
Tell the customer you will come back to them with the confirmed information so they are not left without an answer.
You worked with the delivery team instead of deciding the date on your own.
Contact the delivery team to find out the available dates.
You gave the customer confirmed information only.
Give the customer confirmed information only, without estimates of your own.
You did not promise the customer a date before the delivery team confirmed it.
Do not promise a date before the delivery team confirms it.
You started by apologising to the customer politely.
Start by apologising to the customer politely, before any explanation.
You explained the confirmed information about the order to the customer.
Explain the latest confirmed information about the order to the customer, without unconfirmed promises.
You escalated the problem to the person in charge so it is followed up.
Escalate the problem to the person in charge when needed so it gets solved.
You documented what you noticed about the state of the packaging.
Document what you noticed about the state of the packaging before any other step.
You informed the person in charge about the possible damage.
Inform the person in charge about the possible damage so they decide the next step.
You did not hide the problem.
Do not hide the problem from the team or the customer.
You stopped at the mismatch and did not act before verifying.
Do not complete the delivery before checking the mismatch between the details.
You contacted the relevant department to verify.
Contact the department responsible for the order to verify the details.
You acted after the correct details were confirmed.
Act only after the relevant department confirms the correct details.
